old_caption: The video captures a mechanical experiment set up on a workbench. A transparent rectangular container is positioned beneath a hydraulic press, which features a black cylinder with yellow diagonal stripes for safety. The background consists of a green wall adorned with orange warning signs. Initially, the container appears empty. As the video progresses, a blue substance begins to emerge from the right side of the container, indicating some form of reaction or release. The substance spreads outwards, creating a visually striking contrast against the clear plastic. The hydraulic press remains stationary throughout the sequence, suggesting that it may have been used to initiate the process. The scene is devoid of any human presence, focusing solely on the interaction between the mechanical components and the blue substance.

caption: The video captures a lab view: a plastic-wrapped translucent block on a metal table, a black cylinder banded with yellow hazard stripes and a chrome rod above it, against a green wall with three lightning-bolt signs. The block, cylinder, and camera stay put. After a still interval, a faint blue wisp appears at the block's right edge near the cylinder base, and the chrome rod's top cap drops into view. A blue jet streams leftward through the side fitting, swelling into a rounded blob on a thin stem. Inside, the mass splits into two lobes, re-coalesces, and sprouts a leftward bud that grows then recedes. A separate stream leaks down the side, spreading into a puddle on the metal base. The blue material deforms in place rather than crossing the block. The injection keeps morphing as the clip ends, with no visible operator.

review_issues.quote: a chrome rod to its right
review_issues.problem: The chrome rod rises vertically out of the top of the black cylinder (it is above the cylinder, not to its right); the whole cylinder-and-rod assembly sits to the right of the block.

review_issues.quote: no visible operator or piston motion behind it
review_issues.problem: The chrome piston rod's top cap is absent in frames 1–9 (t=0.00–0.64) but appears at the top of the rod from t=0.72 onward, i.e. the rod visibly shifts downward as the event begins, so an absolute denial of piston motion is inaccurate.
